title: StochasticTwoSidedPL.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective may be nonconvex in x and nonconcave in y; neither convexity nor concavity is required. Both partial gradients are globally L-Lipschitz with respect to the sum of the two variable norms.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticTwoSidedPL.lean: spec.admissible, partial-gradient smoothness and PL inequalities.

problem_class.label: pl
problem_class.details: Uniform two-sided PL inequalities: 2μx(f(x,y)−f(x′,y)) ≤ ‖∇x f(x,y)‖² and 2μy(f(x,y′)−f(x,y)) ≤ ‖∇y f(x,y)‖² for all x,x′,y,y′. Public parameters satisfy 0 < μx,μy ≤ L.

problem_class.label: saddle_point
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimax optimization min_x Φ(x), where Φ(x)=max_y f(x,y). Every inner maximization is attained. The output is a pair (x,y).
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticTwoSidedPL.lean: maxValue, minimaxValue, spec.admissible inner-attainment condition, and spec.Output.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call requests either an x-gradient sample or a y-gradient sample at a supplied pair. Samples are unbiased, with independent identically distributed seeds across calls. No function values, sample-index access, or reuse of a seed across queries is supplied. Oracle cost counts every partial-gradient call under a fixed budget.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticTwoSidedPL.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible oracle answer and infinitePi law, IsUnbiasedOracle.unbiased; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For each partial-gradient oracle and every query z, E‖Gx(z,ω)−∇x f(z)‖² ≤ σ² and E‖Gy(z,ω)−∇y f(z)‖² ≤ σ². Measurability, integrability, and integrability of the squared errors are required; σ ≥ 0 is public.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The primal space E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space. The dual space F is a complete, second-countable real inner-product space and may be infinite-dimensional. Both have Borel measurable structures.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticTwoSidedPL.lean: Params.finiteE, Params.linearE, Params.linearF, Params.completeF, Params.countableF, Params.borelE, and Params.borelF.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: All Params are public, including L, μx, μy, σ, Δ, ε and the starting pair. The objective and oracle witnesses are hidden. Initialization satisfies 2Φ(x0)−Φ*−f(x0,y0)+‖∇x f(x0,y0)‖²/L ≤ Δ, with Δ ≥ 0 and ε > 0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticTwoSidedPL.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.valid, and spec.admissible initialization inequality.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned pair (x̂,ŷ) must satisfy E[(Φ(x̂)−Φ*)+(Φ(x̂)−f(x̂,ŷ))] ≤ ε, where Φ*=inf_x Φ(x). This controls the sum of primal objective suboptimality and inner-maximization suboptimality, rather than a gradient norm or distance.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The output must be measurable and its combined gap integrable. The ε guarantee is in expectation over algorithm randomness and the independent oracle-seed sequence; no high-probability or almost-sure accuracy guarantee is required.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticTwoSidedPL.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence product probability measure.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Smooth two-sided PL minimax optimization with unbiased independent bounded-variance gradient samples and expected objective-gap accuracy is an established problem formulation. The Hilbert-space dual and augmented initialization bound specify its scope without changing the underlying benchmark.

descriptionHtml:
Stochastic Smoothed AGDA under Two-Sided PL

We consider infx∈Esupy∈Ff(x,y) for f:E×F→R, where E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and F is a separable real Hilbert space. The partial gradients are jointly Lipschitz and satisfy two-sided Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequalities; each inner maximum is attained, and the given initial pair satisfies a bounded potential condition. Each oracle call returns an unbiased, bounded-variance estimate of one partial gradient using a fresh independent sample. Stochastic smoothed alternating gradient descent–ascent (AGDA) must return (x¯,y¯) with E[2Φ(x¯)−Φ∗−f(x¯,y¯)]≤ε, where Φ(x)=supy∈Ff(x,y), Φ∗=infx∈EΦ(x), ε>0, and the expectation includes sampling and algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Esupy∈Ff(x,y). Use the inner-product norms on E and F, and the product norm ∥(x,y)∥1=∥x∥+∥y∥. Fix a starting pair (x0,y0)∈E×F and parameters 0<μx≤L,0<μy≤L,σ≥0,Δ≥0,ε>0. The algorithm receives E, F, the measurable sample space Ω, all six scalar parameters, and (x0,y0); the objective and the sampling distribution are accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Partial-gradient smoothness). Each partial function is Fréchet differentiable everywhere. For all x,x′∈E and y,y′∈F, ∥∇xf(x,y)−∇xf(x′,y′)∥≤L(∥x−x′∥+∥y−y′∥),∥∇yf(x,y)−∇yf(x′,y′)∥≤L(∥x−x′∥+∥y−y′∥).

Assumption 2 (Two-sided Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequalities). For every x,x′∈E and y,y′∈F, 2μx(f(x,y)−f(x′,y))≤∥∇xf(x,y)∥2,2μy(f(x,y′)−f(x,y))≤∥∇yf(x,y)∥2. For every x∈E, there exists yx∈F such that f(x,y′)≤f(x,yx)for every y′∈F.

Assumption 3 (Initial potential). The given starting pair satisfies 2Φ(x0)−Φ∗−f(x0,y0)+∥∇xf(x0,y0)∥2L≤Δ.

Assumption 4 (Stochastic partial-gradient oracle). There is a probability distribution ν on Ω and jointly measurable maps Gx:(E×F)×Ω→E,Gy:(E×F)×Ω→F. For each fixed w=(x,y) and a∈{x,y}, the random vector Ga(w,ξ) is Bochner integrable and its squared error is integrable under ξ∼ν, with Eξ∼ν[Ga(w,ξ)]=∇af(w),Eξ∼ν[∥Ga(w,ξ)−∇af(w)∥2]≤σ2. A query at any w∈E×F selects either partial gradient and returns the corresponding estimate. Calls use independent samples with common distribution ν, independent of the algorithm’s randomness.

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze stochastic smoothed AGDA. Its tuning parameters are r,τx,τy,β∈R and n∈N0. Initialize the auxiliary point by z0=x0. With independent samples ξ0,ξ1,…∼ν, each complete iteration consists of gxt=Gx((xt,yt),ξ2t),xt+1=xt−τx(gxt+r(xt−zt)),gyt=Gy((xt+1,yt),ξ2t+1),yt+1=yt+τygyt,zt+1=zt+β(xt+1−zt). Thus one complete iteration uses two oracle calls, with the ascent query made after the descent update. The parameters and n are chosen from the available inputs.

For the output rule, draw J uniformly from {0,…,n}, independently of the samples. Given a total call budget B∈N0, let T=⌊B/2⌋ be the number of complete iterations. The returned pair is (x¯,y¯)={(xn+J,yn+J),1≤n+J≤T,(x0,y0),otherwise. An unmatched final descent call does not change the returned pair.

The output must be measurable, its combined primal suboptimality and inner-maximization error must be integrable, and it must satisfy EP[(Φ(x¯)−Φ∗)+(Φ(x¯)−f(x¯,y¯))]≤ε, where P is the joint law of J and the independent oracle samples.

comparisonHtml:
Real inner-product spaces E,F, with E finite-dimensional and F complete and second-countable, carry their Borel structures. Partial gradients are L-Lipschitz in ∥x−x′∥+∥y−y′∥; f(⋅,y) and −f(x,⋅) satisfy PL inequalities against every competitor, with 0<μx,μy≤L. Every maximization in y is attained. Jointly measurable partial-gradient oracles are unbiased, integrable, and have integrable squared errors of expectation at most σ2; calls use independent samples with common probability law p. The setup restricts algorithms to stochastic Smoothed-AGDA. Given σ,Δ≥0 and ε>0, the target is ∫[Φ(x^)−Φ∗+Φ(x^)−f(x^,y^)]dP≤ε, with measurable output and integrable gap; P includes the sample stream and output randomization.

Stochastic two-sided PL minimax optimization: StochasticTwoSidedPL.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) StochasticTwoSidedPLSmoothedAgda (Ours) (review) O([L2μxμy+L3σ2μx2μy2ε]ℓ)
(2) Derived bound: restarted Smoothed-AGDA (Yang et al. 2022), Thm. 4.1 plus two-sided PL; Euclidean spaces

O(L2ℓμxμy+L3σ2μx2μy2ε)

Conditional on deterministic expected-gap bounds remaining valid at random restart points.

 (1): Matches deterministic rate; extends F to Hilbert space. Single-run potential-PL analysis and formalization; no complexity gain on the Euclidean overlap. (1): Extra factor ℓ in the noise term, conditional on the stated restart bounds.
(3) Stoc-AGDA (Yang et al. 2020), Thm. 3.3; Euclidean spaces, attained minima and a saddle point O(1+L3D0μxμy2ε+L5σ2μx2μy4ε) (1): Noise term smaller by κy2/ℓ when ℓ<κy2, for the shared expected-gap target; not an identical-output speedup. (1): Random second-half iterate instead of last iterate; needs σ,ε,Δ in addition. Its initialization bound includes ∥∇xf(x0,y0)∥2/L.
(4) Warm-started Stoc-AGDA (Yang et al. 2020), Thms. 3.1, 3.3 and Remark 3; Euclidean spaces, attained minima and a saddle point

O(L3ℓμxμy2+L5σ2μx2μy4ε)

Includes the constant-step warm start; uses the common initial bound D0≤Δ.

 (1): Deterministic term κxκyℓ instead of κxκy2ℓ; noise gain κy2/ℓ when ℓ<κy2. (1): Random iterate instead of last iterate. Noise term loses when ℓ>κy2; no uniform dominance.
(5) FESS-GDA (Shen et al. 2024), Thm. 3.5, M=1; Euclidean spaces, attained minima and a saddle point Distance target: E[∥xT−x∗∥2+∥yT−y∗∥2]≤δ2. Rates are not comparable to the gap target. (1): Scope: no saddle-point existence assumption. No established complexity comparison across these accuracy criteria. (1): Does not provide the distance guarantee of (5).

Abbr: Φ(x)=maxyf(x,y), Φ∗=infxΦ(x); D0=2Φ(x0)−Φ∗−f(x0,y0); Δ≥D0+∥∇xf(x0,y0)∥2/L; ℓ=1+log⁡(1+Δ/ε); κx=L/μx, κy=L/μy. Costs count individual partial-gradient calls, including calls to each branch. δ is distance accuracy, (x∗,y∗) a saddle point, and M the client count.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Uniform
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space
import Mathlib.Probability.ProductMeasure

namespace OracleTemplate

noncomputable def stochasticSmoothedAgda {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F] (r τx τy β : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (x0 : E) (y0 : F) :
    Algorithm ((E × F) ⊕ (E × F)) (E ⊕ F) (E × F) where
  Seed := Fin (n + 1)
  law := ⟨(PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin (n + 1))).toMeasure, inferInstance⟩
  State := Fin (n + 1) × ℕ × E × F × E × (E × F)
  initial j := (j, 0, x0, y0, x0, (x0, y0))
  query s := (0, if s.2.1 % 2 = 0 then Sum.inl (s.2.2.1, s.2.2.2.1) else Sum.inr (s.2.2.1, s.2.2.2.1))
  update s reply :=
    match reply with
    | Sum.inl g => (s.1, s.2.1 + 1, s.2.2.1 - τx • (g + r • (s.2.2.1 - s.2.2.2.2.1)), s.2.2.2.1,
        s.2.2.2.2.1, s.2.2.2.2.2)
    | Sum.inr g => (s.1, s.2.1 + 1, s.2.2.1, s.2.2.2.1 + τy • g,
        s.2.2.2.2.1 + β • (s.2.2.1 - s.2.2.2.2.1),
        if (s.2.1 + 1) / 2 = n + (s.1 : ℕ) then (s.2.2.1, s.2.2.2.1 + τy • g) else s.2.2.2.2.2)
  output s := s.2.2.2.2.2

end OracleTemplate

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.StochasticTwoSidedPL

open OracleTemplate

noncomputable def maxValue {E F : Type*} (f : E → F → ℝ) (x : E) : ℝ := ⨆ y, f x y

noncomputable def minimaxValue {E F : Type*} (f : E → F → ℝ) : ℝ := ⨅ x, maxValue f x

structure IsUnbiasedOracle {W V Ω : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
    [MeasurableSpace Ω] (p : Measure Ω) (grad : W → V) (oracle : W → Ω → V) (σ : ℝ)
    [MeasurableSpace W] [MeasurableSpace V] : Prop where
  measurable : Measurable (Function.uncurry oracle)
  integrable : ∀ w, Integrable (oracle w) p
  unbiased : ∀ w, ∫ ω, oracle w ω ∂p = grad w
  variance_integrable : ∀ w, Integrable (fun ω => ‖oracle w ω - grad w‖ ^ 2) p
  variance : ∀ w, ∫ ω, ‖oracle w ω - grad w‖ ^ 2 ∂p ≤ σ ^ 2

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  F : Type u
  [normedF : NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [linearF : InnerProductSpace ℝ F]
  [completeF : CompleteSpace F]
  [measurableF : MeasurableSpace F]
  [borelF : BorelSpace F]
  [countableF : SecondCountableTopology F]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  μx : ℝ
  μy : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E
  y0 : F

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.finiteE Params.measurableE Params.borelE
  Params.normedF Params.linearF Params.completeF Params.measurableF Params.borelF Params.countableF
  Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → p.F → ℝ
  Query p := (p.E × p.F) ⊕ (p.E × p.F)
  Reply p := p.E ⊕ p.F
  Output p := p.E × p.F
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.μx ∧ q.μx ≤ q.L ∧ 0 < q.μy ∧ q.μy ≤ q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (gx : q.E × q.F → q.E) (gy : q.E × q.F → q.F) (Gx : q.E × q.F → q.Ω → q.E)
      (Gy : q.E × q.F → q.Ω → q.F) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω),
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := ⟨Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => (p : Measure q.Ω)), inferInstance⟩
            answer := fun _ (_, w) ω => Sum.elim (fun z => Sum.inl (Gx z ω)) (fun z => Sum.inr (Gy z ω)) w } ∧
      (∀ z : q.E × q.F, HasGradientAt (fun x => f x z.2) (gx z) z.1) ∧
      (∀ z : q.E × q.F, HasGradientAt (fun y => f z.1 y) (gy z) z.2) ∧
      (∀ z z' : q.E × q.F, ‖gx z - gx z'‖ ≤ q.L * (‖z.1 - z'.1‖ + ‖z.2 - z'.2‖)) ∧
      (∀ z z' : q.E × q.F, ‖gy z - gy z'‖ ≤ q.L * (‖z.1 - z'.1‖ + ‖z.2 - z'.2‖)) ∧
      (∀ x x' y, 2 * q.μx * (f x y - f x' y) ≤ ‖gx (x, y)‖ ^ 2) ∧
      (∀ x y y', 2 * q.μy * (f x y' - f x y) ≤ ‖gy (x, y)‖ ^ 2) ∧
      (∀ x, ∃ y, ∀ y', f x y' ≤ f x y) ∧
      IsUnbiasedOracle (p : Measure q.Ω) gx Gx q.σ ∧
      IsUnbiasedOracle (p : Measure q.Ω) gy Gy q.σ ∧
      2 * maxValue f q.x0 - minimaxValue f - f q.x0 q.y0 + ‖gx (q.x0, q.y0)‖ ^ 2 / q.L ≤ q.Δ
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    Integrable (fun ω => (maxValue f (output ω).1 - minimaxValue f) +
      (maxValue f (output ω).1 - f (output ω).1 (output ω).2)) (P : Measure _) ∧
    ∫ ω, (maxValue f (output ω).1 - minimaxValue f) +
      (maxValue f (output ω).1 - f (output ω).1 (output ω).2) ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε
  allowedAlgorithm p A := ∃ (r τx τy β : ℝ) (n : ℕ), A = stochasticSmoothedAgda r τx τy β n p.x0 p.y0

end LongTails.Setups.StochasticTwoSidedPL
